name: Password Filter DLL
description:
Adversaries may register malicious password filter dynamic link libraries (DLLs) into the authentication process to acquire user credentials as they are validated. 

Windows password filters are password policy enforcement mechanisms for both domain and local accounts. Filters are implemented as DLLs containing a method to validate potential passwords against password policies. Filter DLLs can be positioned on local computers for local accounts and/or domain controllers for domain accounts. Before registering new passwords in the Security Accounts Manager (SAM), the Local Security Authority (LSA) requests validation from each registered filter. Any potential changes cannot take effect until every registered filter acknowledges validation. 

Adversaries can register malicious password filters to harvest credentials from local computers and/or entire domains. To perform proper validation, filters must receive plain-text credentials from the LSA. A malicious password filter would receive these plain-text credentials every time a password request is made.(Citation: Carnal Ownage Password Filters Sept 2013)

references.description: Fuller, R. (2013, September 11). Stealing passwords every time they change. Retrieved November 21, 2017.

strategies.name: Detect Malicious Password Filter DLL Registration

analytics.name: Analytic 1303
analytics.guidance: Detects suspicious registration of new password filter DLLs into the authentication process. Correlates registry modifications to LSASS Notification Packages with subsequent DLL creation and loading events. Observes anomalous file placement of DLLs in system directories followed by LSASS loading the new filter during logon/password change activity.

tuning.description: Specific registry path monitored for modification (e.g., HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Notification Packages).
Known and approved password filter DLLs; deviations from baseline may indicate malicious injection.
Time window for correlating registry modification, file creation, and module load events.
Expected directories for legitimate password filter DLLs; anomalous paths may signal compromise.

software.name: Remsec
software.description: [Remsec](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0125) harvests plain-text credentials as a password filter registered on domain controllers.(Citation: Kaspersky ProjectSauron Full Report)

references.description: Kaspersky Lab's Global Research & Analysis Team. (2016, August 9). The ProjectSauron APT. Retrieved August 17, 2016.

actors.name: Strider
actors.description: [Strider](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0041) has registered its persistence module on domain controllers as a Windows LSA (Local System Authority) password filter to acquire credentials any time a domain, local user, or administrator logs in or changes a password.(Citation: Kaspersky ProjectSauron Full Report)

references.description: Kaspersky Lab's Global Research & Analysis Team. (2016, August 9). The ProjectSauron APT. Retrieved August 17, 2016.

actors.name: OilRig
actors.description: [OilRig](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049) has registered a password filter DLL in order to drop malware.(Citation: Trend Micro Earth Simnavaz October 2024)

references.description: Fahmy, M. et al. (2024, October 11). Earth Simnavaz (aka APT34) Levies Advanced Cyberattacks Against Middle East. Retrieved November 27, 2024.

actors.name: MirrorFace
actors.description: [MirrorFace](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1054) has used a tool named MRSAStealer as a password filter to collect credentials on password changes.(Citation: ESET MirrorFace DEC 2022)

references.description: Breitenbacher, D. (2022, December 14). Unmasking MirrorFace: Operation LiberalFace targeting Japanese political entities. Retrieved April 17, 2026.

mitigations.name: Operating System Configuration
mitigations.description: Ensure only valid password filters are registered. Filter DLLs must be present in Windows installation directory (C:\Windows\System32\ by default) of a domain controller and/or local computer with a corresponding entry in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\Notification Packages.

candidates.name: Install Additional Authentication Packages
candidates.description:
lsass.exe loads all DLLs specified by the Authentication Packages REG_MULTI_SZ value.
Uses PowerShell to install and register a password filter DLL. Requires a reboot and administrative privileges.
The binary in bin is https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file/95140c1ad39fd632d1c1300b246293297aa272ce6035eecc3da56e337200221d/detection
Source is in src folder. 
This does require a reboot to see the filter loaded into lsass.exe. 
It does require Administrative privileges to import the clean registry values back into LSA, it is possible you may have to manually do this after for cleanup.
